payload.summary: PhysicsLabStudioHarness owns a singleton RealizedLab through its private current closure, but get() returns the raw RealizedLab including its public destroy() capability. A caller can therefore destroy the owned lab without clearing harness ownership, leaving current bound to a dead handle.
payload.impact: After out-of-band destroy(), Harness.get() still returns the destroyed handle and Harness.start() rejects a replacement as already owned even though the canonical physical/runtime lab has been disposed. This can poison a Studio validation/evidence session until Harness.stop() is explicitly called, and it weakens the intended single-owner teardown boundary by exposing lifecycle authority outside the harness.
sourceProof: main@ae83c0ef470eb2e73d99be41fd3561ede30c40e1 PhysicsLabStudioHarness.start() assigns the raw PhysicsLabRealizer.realize() result to private current; get() returns current directly

the RealizedLab public type includes destroy, and PhysicsLabRealizer.destroy() marks the handle destroyed, destroys its model, clears representations, and disposes runtime without any callback into PhysicsLabStudioHarness
PhysicsLabStudioHarness.stop() is the only harness path that calls active.destroy() and then clears current

stale teardown test PR #307 verifies start duplicate fencing, stop destroy-before-clear ordering, restart teardown, and bootstrap order, but does not test or prevent an external caller invoking get().destroy() and desynchronizing current
payload.sourceLevelRepro: In Studio-server context by source inspection: local lab = assert(PhysicsLabStudioHarness.get()); lab.destroy(); PhysicsLabStudioHarness.get() still returns that same destroyed table because current is unchanged; a subsequent PhysicsLabStudioHarness.start(workspace) reaches the current ~= nil ownership assertion. No Studio execution is claimed.
payload.nonDuplicate: PR #307 is specifically teardown ownership but only locks harness-owned stop/restart sequencing. Repository PR/issue search found no existing direct-destroy capability or stale-current repair.
recommendedClosure: keep lifecycle authority centralized: callers that only need diagnostics/runtime access should not receive an uncoordinated destroy capability
use the narrowest production-worthy seam, such as a harness-owned facade without destroy or a destruction path that atomically clears the matching current owner
add a source/pure regression that an external handle cannot leave current pointing at a destroyed lab and that replacement remains deterministic
preserve stop idempotency, restart ordering, exactly-one-lab ownership, and existing Studio-only/server-only assertions
do not translate source closure into two-client or Studio evidence PASS
